scripts.//typecheck:apps: apps/landing only. apps/storybook is typechecked by its build (yarn storybook:build), NOT by vue-tsc: its tsconfig targets the Vite builder, so a standalone vue-tsc reports 1,671 environment errors -- 699 of them TS5097 against the repo's own mandated .ts import extensions (CLAUDE.md rule 5) and 341 TS2307 for bundler-only modules. See docs/storybook-decisions.md.
scripts.typecheck:all: tsc --noEmit -p packages/tokens/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/contracts/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/testing/tsconfig.json && vue-tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.json && vue-tsc --noEmit -p packages/compat/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/codemods/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/mcp/tsconfig.json && yarn typecheck:apps
scripts.//lint: packages/ AND both apps (TASK-FREE2-01). --max-warnings 0: the baseline is zero errors and zero warnings, so a new warning fails CI rather than accreting into a 'known baseline' everyone ignores. Generated output is excluded via eslint.config.js `ignores`, not CLI globs.
scripts.build: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/contracts build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/testing build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/core build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/compat build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/codemods build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/nuxt build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/mcp build
scripts.//generate:ownership: TASK-OSS-P0-01. Regenerates packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json -- the single deterministic answer to "who owns DzFoo?" that the resolver, the Nuxt module, and the cross-tier ownership map consume. It REPORTS: symbols no authority can classify are emitted as `unclassified` with their evidence, never guessed from a Dz prefix. Core has one tier, so :core is an alias kept for symmetry with Pro.
scripts.//generate:ownership:map: TASK-OSS-P0-02. Merges a Core and a Pro ownership manifest into one exact-name lookup. The Pro input is a FILE produced by a Pro checkout (Pro TASK-GOV-01) -- Core never reads Pro source. Exits non-zero on any cross-tier name collision: a collision is resolved only by a checked-in decision in packages/tooling/src/ownership/collision-decisions.json that names an ADR. Example: yarn generate:ownership:map -- --core packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --pro ../dzup-ui-pro/packages/pro/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --out /tmp/ownership-map.json
scripts.//generate:readme-facts: TASK-OSS-P2-02. Rewrites the marked fact regions of README.md from package.json and the ownership manifest. The package table was hand-typed and five of its six rows named a version the package had already moved past, while two publishable packages were missing entirely. Complements apps/landing build-counts.ts, which owns the separate claims:generated region of the same file.
scripts.//validate:hardcoded-strings: TASK-OSS-P4-03. Fails on a user-visible string a component hard-codes: a static aria-label in a template (nobody can change it -- there were 54), or a literal default on a *Text/*Label/*Placeholder prop (only changeable one instance at a time -- there were 39). Reads the <template> block only, so JSDoc @example strings are not swept up. Mark a line `hardcoded-string-ok: <reason>` when the value genuinely is not language; the reason lives at the string, not in a list.
scripts.//generate:rtl-matrix: TASK-OSS-P4-05. Rewrites packages/core/docs/rtl-matrix.md from the `rtl` field each component declares in its anatomy, so the table cannot drift from the declarations the way a hand-maintained one does.
scripts.//validate:rtl: TASK-OSS-P4-05. A component that declares `rtl: { mirrors: 'layout' }` must not use physical left/right utilities in its variants -- and the generated matrix must match the declarations. A deliberate physical case says `rtl-physical-ok` in the file with its reason (code blocks, `align="left"`, a sheet side the author named). Source-level only: whether `margin-inline-start` resolves to the correct physical edge needs an engine that does layout, which is `expectRtlComputed` in the Playwright lane.
scripts.//generate:quality-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-01. Joins the ownership manifest, the tier rules in @dzup-ui/contracts, and the reviewed assignment in packages/tooling/src/quality/component-tiers.ts into packages/core/docs/quality-matrix.json -- the single answer to "what evidence does DzX owe", which every other P5 packet reads instead of re-deriving it.
scripts.//validate:quality-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-01. The tier assignment is the one handwritten inventory here, so it is the one most able to drift: this fails when a public component has no tier, when a tier is assigned to a symbol that stopped being public, when a Tier C/D or `custom` pattern carries no reason, when a WCAG id or an exception names something outside the catalog, when a component renders teleported content without declaring the trait, when a component's own anatomy contradicts the assignment, or when the generated matrix is stale.
scripts.//generate:matrix-targets: TASK-OSS-P5-03. Rewrites e2e/matrix/targets.generated.ts from quality-matrix.json and the story corpus, so the browser matrix covers every Tier B-D component the moment it becomes public. A component with no story is emitted with `story: null` and reported as unrun, never dropped.
scripts.//generate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Writes one e2e/at-matrix/{Component}.md per Tier B-D component and the index.json the capability matrix reads. The generator owns everything ABOVE the results marker and never rewrites a recorded run below it.
scripts.//validate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Fails on a malformed or unevidenced row -- an unknown AT pair, an unrecognised result, a `pass` with no versions/tester/date/commit behind it, or an index that disagrees with the markdown. Unrun and stale cells are REPORTED, not failed: every row in a new matrix starts unrun, and a gate that failed on that would be switched off the day it landed.
scripts.//generate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06. Joins the quality matrix, the ownership manifest, the Story DoD report, the AT index, the perf baselines and the browser-matrix ledger into packages/core/docs/capability-matrix.json, plus the narrowed projection the Storybook page imports. One row per public component, one cell per evidence row it owes, marked pass/present/stale/unrun/excepted.
scripts.//validate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06. Fails when the committed matrix is stale, and when a Tier D component carries an `unrun` cell with no artifact behind it -- a Tier D gap is a security gap and does not get to be an empty cell. Stale cells and absent inputs are reported by name, never folded into a count.
scripts.//validate:story-dod-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-02. The triaged half of validate:story-dod: it joins the 366 advisory items to the risk tiers and holds a per-check CEILING on the ones a tier actually requires. The ceiling only falls. A ceiling rather than zero because promoting the checks outright would land 51 red items on a green build, which this packet's own stop condition forbids. `--all` lists the open items; `--write` lowers the ceiling after a fix.
scripts.//perf:capture: TASK-OSS-P5-05. Re-measures every performance baseline: the runtime benchmarks over >= 5 separate processes (cross-process variance is where the two recorded flakes come from) and a tree-shaken fixture build per Tier C/D export. Writes packages/core/perf/baselines.json with the distribution AND the threshold it earned -- or `not yet measurable` when the spread swamps the signal. An owner action, never automatic: a suite that wrote its own baseline every run would ratchet upward forever and call it a budget.
scripts.//validate:package-names: TASK-OSS-P1-01. Fails when a retired package name reappears outside the paths allowed to record history. Config is data: packages/tooling/scripts/retired-package-names.json. A file that must name a retired package -- a migration note, a test asserting it is never emitted -- says so with a `retired-name-ok: <reason>` comment on the line or the line above.
scripts.//validate:doc-snippets: TASK-OSS-P1-04. Every install snippet marked with a fixture comment must equal the fixture file a test actually builds. Documentation nothing executes drifts, and this repo has paid that bill twice: the docs advertised includePro against a package that never existed, and the module loaded a stylesheet path the tokens package does not export.
scripts.//validate:engines: TASK-OSS-P2-01 / ADR-18. The declared Node floor must (a) be the same number in package.json, .nvmrc and every CI workflow, and (b) be satisfiable by the dependencies the mandatory gates load. It was neither: engines said >=20.0.0 while vite@7 and jsdom@29 require ^20.19.0, and every CI job requested a floating major that resolves to the newest 20.x -- so the floor was a claim nothing ran on.
scripts.//validate:adr-references: TASK-OSS-P3-01, ADR-19. Every ADR-NN cited in source or prose must resolve to a document in docs/adr/ or to an entry in packages/tooling/scripts/adr-registry.json -- a ratcheted debt ledger of the 14 decisions this repository cites but has never written down. The set may only shrink. Put `adr-example-ok:` on a line to exempt an id that is an example rather than a citation.
scripts.validate:all: yarn typecheck && yarn lint && yarn validate:boundaries && yarn validate:interaction-contract && yarn validate:contract-parity && yarn validate:hardcoded-strings && yarn validate:rtl && yarn validate:quality-tiers && yarn validate:story-status && yarn validate:story-dod && yarn validate:story-dod-tiers && yarn validate:at-matrix && yarn validate:capability-matrix && yarn validate:tokens && yarn validate:exports && yarn validate:ownership && yarn validate:package-names && yarn validate:doc-snippets && yarn validate:engines && yarn validate:adr-references && yarn validate:readme-facts && yarn validate:externals && yarn validate:dts && yarn validate:changelog && yarn validate:peers && yarn validate:licenses
scripts.//test:nuxt-fixtures: TASK-OSS-P1-03. Real Nuxt consumer apps, installed from packed tarballs and staged OUTSIDE this repository -- a fixture kept inside the monorepo resolves the repo's own nuxt/nitropack/vite through Node's upward directory walk and stops being a consumer test. Three steps because one install is ~800 packages and one build is ~60s: :pack (yarn pack + stage), :install (npm install each), then the assertions. Set DZUP_PRO_TARBALL to a tarball produced by a Pro checkout to include the core-pro fixture; without it that fixture reports `unrun`, not `skipped`.
scripts.test:e2e:functional: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/a11y e2e/components e2e/smoke
scripts.//test:e2e:matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-03. The three-engine x five-condition lane over every Tier B-D component: chromium/firefox/webkit x {default, forced-colors, reduced-motion, rtl, touch, zoom-400}. Results are per cell, not an aggregate pass count -- set PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT to emit the report the capability matrix reads. Tier A stays in the single chromium lane e2e/components already gives it. Pass --project=matrix-webkit-rtl (or --shard) to run one cell.
scripts.test:e2e:matrix: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/matrix
scripts.//test:e2e:matrix:prebuilt: The same lane against an ALREADY-built apps/storybook/storybook-static. Separate because one Storybook build is ~4 minutes and the lane is normally re-run many times against one build.
scripts.test:e2e:visual: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && DZUP_GALLERY=1 yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/visual --max-failures=1
scripts.//test:e2e:landing: TASK-FREE3-06. The landing's own Playwright suite (apps/landing/e2e): the five core flows, the pixel/blank-page guards, the hero baselines, and a Pixel 7 project. `:preview` swaps the dev server for `vite preview` over apps/landing/dist -- that is what CI runs, so the browser drives the artifact users actually receive. Both scripts invoke @playwright/test's own CLI rather than the `playwright` bin shim; see the note in apps/landing/playwright.config.ts.
scripts.//test:responsive:landing: The block responsive-certification sweep: every block at each breakpoint in both text directions. Kept as its own script because it is the one spec worth running alone against a single block change; the full `test:e2e:landing` run includes it. `:ci` pins workers and fails the run on a flaky pass rather than letting a retry launder it.
scripts.storybook:install: yarn install && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/storybook exec playwright install chromium
